terms: 1. Parties and commencement

This Joint Venture Agreement (Agreement) is entered into on [DATE] between Nexora International, with its business address at Herengracht 208, 1016 BS Amsterdam, the Netherlands, registration number [CONFIRMED REGISTRATION NUMBER], represented by [NAME / TITLE] (Nexora or Party A); and [PARTY B LEGAL NAME], incorporated in [COUNTRY], registration number [NUMBER], registered address [ADDRESS], represented by [NAME / TITLE] (Party B). Each is a Party and together the Parties.
Party B's details shall correspond to its approved portal company profile. Before signature, each Party must confirm its legal identity, registration details and representative's authority. The use of Nexora International as the displayed party name does not dispense with identifying its contracting legal entity in the signed record.
2. Contractual cooperation

The Parties establish a contractual, project-specific joint venture to originate, develop and execute the commercial project described in Schedule A (Project). No separate company, equity interest, employment relationship, agency or general authority to represent the other Party is created by this Agreement. Neither Party may bind the other or incur liabilities in its name without a separate express written mandate.
Each Party contracts with third parties in its own identified legal capacity unless a separately approved external contract states otherwise. They shall not operate under a common firm name without first reviewing and documenting the applicable legal structure. Mandatory legal rules and the actual manner of cooperation determine any partnership classification and third-party liability, irrespective of these statements.
3. Project approval and document priority

This Agreement takes effect only when signed by both authorised representatives. No trading, funding or other Project commitment is authorised until Schedule A is completed and signed by both Parties. Additional projects require separate signed schedules. Portal registration, submission of a proposed percentage or an approval notification alone does not execute this Agreement.
Priority is: (i) signed amendments expressly identifying the affected provisions; (ii) Schedule A for its specified commercial variables; (iii) this Agreement; and (iv) expressly incorporated documents. Schedule A cannot silently override the liability, compliance or dispute provisions. Existing confidentiality or commission agreements remain effective unless expressly varied; no amount may be recovered twice.
4. Scope and responsibilities

The Project description must identify products or services, territory, counterparties where known, deliverables, milestones, responsibilities and completion criteria. Each Party shall perform its allocated tasks with reasonable professional care, provide accurate material information and promptly disclose delays or conflicts. Neither Party guarantees a transaction, financing, profit or third-party performance. Exclusivity exists only if expressly limited by activity, counterparties and duration in Schedule A and lawful under applicable competition rules.
5. Decision-making and authority

Each Party appoints one authorised Project representative. Routine coordination may be delegated to the Project lead within the signed budget and mandate. The following require both Parties' prior written approval: external contracts and material amendments; pricing and payment terms; expenditure outside the approved budget; borrowing, security or guarantees; appointment or payment of brokers; related-party arrangements; settlement of claims; changes to bank instructions; and any change to scope, funding or profit allocation.
No percentage gives unilateral voting or signing authority. Silence is not approval. The Project lead maintains a decision log and circulates material decisions and documents to both representatives. A change of representative must be notified in writing with evidence of authority.
6. Contributions and funding

Schedule A must specify each Party's cash, assets, services and other contributions, their agreed value where relevant, due dates, ownership and whether amounts are reimbursable, repayable advances or non-repayable contributions. Neither Party must provide additional finance or guarantees beyond its express signed commitment. A shortfall requires a new jointly signed funding decision; it does not automatically dilute a profit percentage.
Third-party funding, security and finance charges require prior mutual approval. Neither Party may pledge the other's assets or Project receivables without express authority. Funds must be paid only to verified accounts in the entitled contracting Party's name, or to an expressly approved regulated escrow arrangement.
7. Budgets, expenses and losses

Only reasonable, documented Project expenses within the mutually approved budget are recoverable. Unbudgeted costs require advance written approval. Each Party bears its ordinary overhead, staff costs, travel and business-development costs unless specific recovery is approved in Schedule A. No hidden markup or related-party charge is permitted.
The Parties must separately select a loss allocation and maximum funding exposure in Schedule A. Profit percentages do not automatically allocate losses. A Party is not obliged to replenish a deficit beyond its agreed contribution or approved funding commitment, except for liabilities arising from its breach or another applicable provision. This internal allocation does not limit lawful claims by third parties. If no loss arrangement is selected, the Project must not commence.
8. Accounts and control of funds

Schedule A identifies the contracting, invoicing and collection Party and the account or escrow arrangements. Collection in one Party's account does not create a separate legal trust or shield funds from insolvency. Where segregation or security is material, a suitable escrow or security arrangement must be completed before funding.
The collection Party shall maintain a separate Project ledger, reconcile receipts and payments monthly and provide both Parties with supporting statements. Payments above the approval threshold in Schedule A require both representatives' documented approval before release. Bank-detail changes require independent verification through a previously verified contact channel. Cash payments and payments to unrelated third parties are prohibited unless lawful and expressly approved by both Parties.
9. Net Distributable Profit

Net Distributable Profit means Project revenue actually received in cleared funds, excluding VAT and similar collected taxes, less: (a) mutually approved, documented direct Project costs; (b) approved third-party charges and commissions; (c) customer refunds, credits and actual Project bad-debt losses to the extent not already excluded from receipts; (d) taxes legally payable at Project level; and (e) reasonable, specifically documented reserves approved by both Parties for outstanding Project obligations.
No deduction is permitted for general overhead, internal profit margins, salaries, time charges, corporate income tax of either Party or related-party costs unless expressly approved in Schedule A. No expense, principal repayment or loss may be counted twice. Each Party bears its own tax on its share.
10. Waterfall and selected percentages

Cleared Project cash shall be applied in this order: (i) statutory payments and due external Project obligations; (ii) approved reserves; (iii) repayment of expressly repayable Project advances in the priority agreed in Schedule A; and (iv) distribution of Net Distributable Profit.
The Parties shall select Nexora: [___]% and Party B: [___]%. Each percentage must be greater than zero and below 100, with no more than two decimal places; together they must equal exactly 100%. No default percentage applies. These are contractual rights to the defined Project profit, not shares in either company. Funding, losses and voting rights are governed separately.
Changes apply only through an amendment signed by both Parties and shall state the effective date and treatment of already accrued rights. Repayment of loan principal is a cash-waterfall item, not a second deduction when calculating profit.
11. Statements and distributions

Within 15 Business Days after each calendar month, the collection Party shall deliver a Project statement showing receipts, expenses, reserves, advances and the calculation of distributable profit. Uncontested amounts lawfully available for distribution shall be paid within 10 Business Days after the statement, subject to due third-party obligations and approved reserves. A final account shall be issued within 30 Business Days after Project completion, with later receipts or liabilities accounted for promptly.
A Party may object with reasons within 20 Business Days of receipt. This administrative period does not waive fraud, concealed errors or statutory rights. The undisputed balance shall still be paid. Reserves must be reviewed monthly and released when no longer reasonably required.
12. Records, audit and tax

Both Parties shall retain adequate Project records for at least seven years or any longer mandatory period. On reasonable notice, each may inspect relevant records through an independent professional subject to confidentiality, no more than once annually unless there is a reasonable concern about an error or breach. Unrelated confidential information may be redacted without concealing Project evidence.
Accounting disagreements may be referred jointly to an independent Dutch chartered accountant for expert determination of calculations only, subject to applicable Dutch rules on binding advice; legal disputes remain for the court. Costs are shared equally unless an error exceeding 5% against the requesting Party is established, in which case the responsible Party bears reasonable review costs. VAT treatment, invoicing and any legally required withholding shall be applied correctly; withholding evidence must be supplied. No tax gross-up applies unless expressly agreed.
13. Due diligence and lawful conduct

Each Party shall provide reasonable company, beneficial-ownership, authority and source-of-funds information required for lawful due diligence, and promptly report material changes. Performance is conditional on completion of applicable checks. Each Party shall comply with applicable sanctions, export controls, anti-bribery, anti-money-laundering, tax, competition and trade laws and obtain licences required for its role.
No Party shall offer improper payments, conceal beneficial ownership, misdescribe goods or origin, facilitate sanctions evasion or exchange competitively sensitive information beyond what is lawfully necessary for the Project. Neither is required to perform an unlawful act. A substantiated compliance concern permits proportionate suspension while investigated, with prompt notice where legally permitted. An unlawful obligation shall not be performed merely because the other Party approves it.
14. Confidentiality and publicity

Confidential Information includes non-public commercial, financial, technical, counterparty, pricing and Project information disclosed in any form. A recipient shall use it only for the Project and disclose it only to personnel, professional advisers and approved financiers with a need to know and equivalent duties. The recipient shall apply reasonable security safeguards.
These duties exclude information demonstrably public without breach, already lawfully held, independently developed or lawfully received without restriction. Legally required disclosure is permitted to the necessary extent, with prior notice where lawful. No Party may use the other's name, logo or Project as a public reference without written consent. Duties survive five years after termination; trade secrets remain protected while qualifying as such. Information must be returned or deleted on request, subject to lawful retention and secure backup limitations.
15. Personal data

Each Party shall comply with applicable data-protection law, including the GDPR where applicable, minimise personal data and use appropriate access controls and security. Each acts as an independent controller for its own compliance and business administration unless the facts require another role. If one processes personal data on behalf of the other, the required Article 28 processing agreement must be concluded before that processing. Any joint-controller arrangement and international transfer safeguards shall likewise be documented where required. A Party shall promptly notify the other of a relevant security incident, without delaying its own statutory notification duties.
16. Intellectual property and introductions

Each Party retains its pre-existing intellectual property. It grants the other only the limited, non-transferable right necessary to use approved materials for this Project during its term. Ownership and permitted use of newly created deliverables must be specified in Schedule A before creation; no implied transfer occurs. Brand use always requires approval.
For 12 months after a documented introduction, neither Party shall knowingly bypass the introducing Party to avoid its agreed remuneration on the specific Project opportunity listed in Schedule B. This does not restrict demonstrable pre-existing relationships, independently sourced business, unsolicited unrelated opportunities or lawful competition. Schedule B must identify the contact and opportunity; no general market or customer allocation is created. Remedies are proven loss and available court relief; no automatic commission or contractual penalty is implied.
17. Warranties, risk and liability

Each Party warrants its authority to enter this Agreement, accuracy of material information to its knowledge after reasonable enquiry, and that it will not knowingly infringe third-party rights in its own supplied materials. Product quality, title, delivery, inspection, insurance and payment risk must be addressed in approved underlying contracts; this Agreement is not a substitute for those contracts.
A Party is liable for loss caused by its attributable breach, subject to reasonable mitigation and, where remediable, a written opportunity to cure. Aggregate contractual liability of each Party per Project is capped at the amount expressly selected in Schedule A. No Project may commence with that field blank. Neither Party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, loss of opportunity or anticipated profit, except amounts expressly owed under the distribution provisions.
The cap and exclusions do not limit payment of due profit shares, approved repayment obligations or committed funding; fraud, wilful misconduct or deliberate recklessness of management; or liability that cannot lawfully be limited. No blanket indemnity for the other's business is granted. Third-party claims must be notified promptly; no settlement binding the other Party is permitted without its consent.
18. Duration, suspension and termination

The framework continues from signature until terminated on 30 days' written notice. Such notice prevents new Projects but does not cancel an existing signed Project, which continues until completed or separately terminated. Either Party may terminate an affected Project for a material breach not cured within 15 Business Days after detailed written notice, or immediately for a non-remediable material breach, fraud or continued unlawful performance. Insolvency-related termination is subject to mandatory law.
Events beyond reasonable control may excuse affected performance while they continue, provided prompt notice and mitigation; lack of funds alone is not such an event. Accrued payment obligations remain due. If the event materially prevents performance for 60 consecutive days, either Party may terminate the affected unperformed portion on written notice.
19. Deadlock and orderly closure

A deadlock shall be escalated to the Parties' senior representatives within 10 Business Days. They shall seek resolution for a further 10 Business Days. Pending resolution, no new disputed commitment may be made; lawful existing obligations and necessary preservation measures continue. If unresolved, either Party may request orderly termination of the affected Project on 20 Business Days' notice, subject to binding external commitments.
On closure, the Parties shall cooperate to collect receivables, fulfil or lawfully exit external contracts, pay approved obligations, release reserves, repay eligible advances and distribute remaining profit under the agreed waterfall. Neither Party gains the other's assets or accrued rights. Confidentiality, records, payment rights, IP, applicable contact protection, liability and dispute provisions survive to the extent necessary.
20. Governing law and general provisions

Dutch law governs this Agreement and its non-contractual obligations. The competent court of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, has exclusive jurisdiction, subject to mandatory jurisdiction rules. Representatives shall first attempt good-faith settlement for 10 Business Days after dispute notice; urgent court relief and limitation-preserving steps remain available.
Notices shall be sent to the designated email addresses in Schedule A and are effective on confirmed delivery, or the next Business Day if sent outside business hours, excluding failed delivery. Business Day means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a Dutch public holiday. Assignment requires the other's prior written consent. Amendments and waivers require both Parties' express written approval; failure to enforce is not waiver. If a provision is invalid, the remaining provisions continue where practicable and the Parties shall agree a lawful replacement reflecting its purpose. This Agreement and its signed schedules contain the entire agreement on their subject matter. Counterparts and reliable electronic signatures are accepted. No signature or contractual version may be replaced by a unilateral portal update. There are no intended third-party beneficiaries.
